definition: Mastery orientation is a tendency to approach personal growth and challenges with a focus on learning, improving, and developing competence and autonomy. In this source, it is presented as the pattern linked to incremental beliefs that people can change, in contrast to a helpless orientation linked to entity beliefs.

reasons: The first sentence adds unsourced glosses (“personal growth and challenges,” “learning, improving, and developing competence and autonomy”) that are not stated in the packet.

The packet supports only the narrower point that mastery orientation is associated with incremental beliefs about change, contrasted with helpless orientation and entity beliefs; the broader behavioral definition is not established here.

The definition describes mastery orientation as “a tendency to approach personal growth and challenges with a focus on learning, improving, and developing competence and autonomy,” but the packet only states that incremental beliefs are associated with a “mastery orientation” and that autonomy and competence motives mediate relationships with well-being; it does not explicitly define mastery orientation in terms of approaching personal growth/challenges or “learning/improving” as the focus.

The definition claims that mastery orientation is “presented as the pattern linked to incremental beliefs … in contrast to a helpless orientation linked to entity beliefs.” While the packet supports the contrast between mastery and helpless orientations in relation to incremental and entity beliefs, the definition’s broader formulation of what mastery orientation entails (learning/improving/personal growth focus) is not supported by the packet.
